rule: A configuration variable whose name ends in _KEY or _KEYS is key material and is classified as a secret. This list is the ONLY exemption, and it is fail-closed: a new *_KEY variable that is not declared here is a secret by default. Inability to prove a name is not key material is not proof that it is not.
why_a_declaration_and_not_a_pattern: The three exemptions below cannot be told apart from real key material by their names. MFA_ALLOW_DERIVED_KEY and MFA_AUDIT_HASH_KEY differ by one word and sit in the same service, yet one is a boolean flag and the other is a hash key. A regex that got both right would be a regex fitted to these thirteen names, which is a list wearing a pattern's clothes. So the exemption is a list, each entry carrying the source line that was read to classify it.
adding_an_entry: Read the code that consumes the variable and record file:line here. A name that merely looks harmless does not qualify -- the evidence is the read, not the reading of the name.

nonsecret.name: JWT_PUBLIC_KEY
nonsecret.reason: Public half of an asymmetric pair. It is the verification side and is meant to be distributable; treating it as a secret would misreport the service's secret surface upward, which is its own kind of dishonesty.
nonsecret.services: actuator-service, auth, erp-bridge, guardrails-engine, local-ai-rag, sahool-platform, supervisor-agent, tts-service, vegetation-analysis-service, video-processor

nonsecret.name: MFA_ALLOW_DERIVED_KEY
nonsecret.reason: Not key material at all -- a boolean opt-in flag. It is read as a truthy string and gates whether a derived key is permitted; it never carries a key.

nonsecret.name: STAGING_PROBE_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY
nonsecret.reason: A deduplication identifier, not a credential. It ships a plaintext default in the source, which a secret could never do.
